pure-announcement.rationale: This is the vendor's own launch post for tapes.dev — 'We're sharing Tapes on GitHub today', install commands, a design-partner call-to-action — and its non-product content is either aspirational roadmap ('we're building toward a future where...') or the proxy-capture mechanism the corpus already holds.

duplicate.rationale: proxy-boundary-session-capture already covers Tapes' capture mechanism (proxy, Merkle DAG, content addressing) but frames it as crash recovery, so the semantic-recall-as-agent-memory purpose here is nominally new to a reader of that concept.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The mechanism is checkable — the open-source repo, docs, and runnable proxy are linked — even though the benefit claims (warm starts, self-healing loops) are asserted rather than evidenced.

durability.rationale: Most of the content is product-specific setup (install script, tapes serve flags, OpenClaw config, Chroma partnership) and unshipped roadmap bullets, which will not describe reality in twelve months even if the underlying preserve-and-recall idea survives.

actionability.rationale: The only concrete actions are product-only steps — curl-install Tapes, run the proxy, edit openclaw.json — rather than guidance that transfers to building session memory with any stack.

atomicity.rationale: The note tells one product story whose core idea — preserve agent sessions and give future sessions semantic recall over them — is stateable in a single paragraph.
